title: Check rsp.GetError(), not just err, after unified-storage search calls
answers: Why did a search failure get treated as 'no results found'?
LIST with a label selector returns 200 with an empty list instead of an error
A duplicate internal ID check or search-backed lookup silently passes when the search actually failed
How should I check the result of a resourcepb search response?
body:
Symptom: a search-backed operation (LIST with selectors, a dedup lookup) returns success/empty instead of failing when the underlying search call actually errored (e.g. the search token lacked a delegated permission).
Root cause: code checked only the Go `err` return of the search call and ignored `rsp.GetError()`, so a failed search with `err == nil` and zero rows looked identical to 'nothing matched'. Seen in pkg/storage/unified/apistore/prepare.go:ensureSingleDeprecatedInternalID before the fix.
Fix pattern: wrap the response with `resource.ErrorFromResponse(rsp.GetError(), err)` (see pkg/storage/unified/resource/errors.go) and treat any non-nil result as a hard failure, not an empty result; also log the error with group/resource so the failure is visible when only logs are available (pkg/storage/unified/resource/list_with_selectors.go:listWithSelectors).
Constraints: applies to any code that calls into resource/search APIs and interprets an empty/zero-row response as 'confirmed no match' — a zero-row response must first be confirmed error-free via ErrorFromResponse before being treated as authoritative.
applies: unified storage (resource/, search/, apistore/) code paths that call search and branch on an empty result
says: Why did a search failure show as empty results instead of an error?
A label filter returned success with no items when search actually failed
How should search failures be distinguished from truly empty search results?
Search-backed lookup silently succeeds even though the search request errored
Why doesn't a permission error in search show up in the results?
search: After calling unified storage search APIs, check both rsp.GetError() and the Go err return; checking only err misses failed searches with err == nil and zero rows that look identical to 'no match found'. Wrap with resource.ErrorFromResponse(rsp.GetError(), err) from pkg/storage/unified/resource/errors.go and treat any non-nil result as hard failure, not empty result; also log the error with group/resource (see list_with_selectors.go:listWithSelectors) for visibility in log-only scenarios. This applies to any code interpreting zero-row responses as 'confirmed no match'—such responses must first be confirmed error-free before treating them as authoritative.
